profile.campus: Digital Realty Chicago (downtown / Elk Grove Village / Franklin Park), IL
profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility ORD10, at 350 East Cermak Road, Chicago, IL 60616, widely known as the Lakeside Technology Center. Digital Realty's own property listing for ORD10, fetched this session, lists the building at 1,005,500 square feet, making it one of the largest single data center buildings in Digital Realty's global portfolio.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building anchors Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint, which also includes 600 South Federal Street downtown and a cluster of suburban buildings in Elk Grove Village and Franklin Park near O'Hare International Airport. Digital Realty markets its Chicago properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Chicago buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage. Illinois has offered data center-specific state tax incentives, administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, that local officials have credited with helping draw large colocation and hyperscale investment to the Chicago metro.

reading.body:
Digital Realty ORD10 is a 1,005,500 square foot colocation building at 350 East Cermak Road in Chicago, widely known as the Lakeside Technology Center. The operator does not publish an IT power capacity figure for this building in its property listing or FY2025 Form 10-K. Without a megawatt rating, the scale of compute this building can host cannot be translated into racks or accelerators.

The building anchors Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint alongside 600 South Federal Street downtown and suburban properties near O'Hare Airport. Digital Realty operates as a colocation landlord, renting space to hyperscalers and other tenants rather than running its own AI training or inference. The operator markets these properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand as part of a global interconnection platform spanning more than 55 metros, 221 wholly owned or consolidated facilities, and 57.6 million square feet worldwide as of December 31, 2025.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, six with published megawatt figures totaling 236 MW according to operator disclosures reviewed by this site. This building ranks seventh in the state by published capacity, though that rank reflects only the six operators who have disclosed figures; the true ranking by actual power draw is unknown. ComEd is the principal electric utility for the metro, and Illinois offers state tax incentives for data center operators that local officials credit with attracting large colocation and hyperscale investment.
